model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different methods, Per-Output and Per-Layer. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled with values ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, while the vertical axis represents perplexity, labeled with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3. The chart features grouped bars, with each group corresponding to a specific sparsity rate and containing two bars: a blue bar representing Per-Output and an orange bar representing Per-Layer. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, with the Per-Output bar positioned first and the Per-Layer bar second in each group. At a sparsity rate of 10%, both Per-Output and Per-Layer have a perplexity of approximately 4. As the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity for both methods remains relatively stable until 60%, where it starts to rise, with Per-Output at around 8 and Per-Layer at around 9; at 70%, Per-Output is at approximately 15 and Per-Layer is at around 30; and at 80%, Per-Output is at around 400 and Per-Layer is at around 900. The bars are sorted in ascending order by sparsity rate, and there is no visual emphasis on any particular bar.
